## [Architecture](/architecture/)

# Architecture

ch3 is authored inside the **scriptc compilable subset**: the whole package lowers statically into a native ELF via `scriptc build --npm-static ch3` with zero deferred sites (100% static coverage on scriptc 0.2.8).

The full document lives in the repo: [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/sigilco/ch3/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md).

Highlights of the subset rules the source obeys:

- `| null` unions only
- Plain records for route data (no function values inside records: handlers live in `App._fns`, nodes carry indices)
- Indexed loops, no recursion for matching (explicit frame stack)
- No `slice`/`concat`/spread on package paths
- Statement-called `res.end()`

One file, `src/index.ts`, holds the whole core: router, context, node adapter.

The generated-dispatch seam (`src/gen.ts`, frozen contract) allows build-time route lowering: [route-contract.md](route-contract.md).


---

## [Benchmarks](/benchmarks/)

# Benchmarks

Shared VM, compare ratios not absolutes. Full matrix, methodology, ceilings (go-chi / axum / mongoose), and a one-command Docker repro: [bench/RESULTS-v2.md](https://github.com/sigilco/ch3/blob/main/bench/RESULTS-v2.md).

| subject | json | pipelined (-c100 -p10) | cold start | RSS after 100k req |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ch3 on node | 0.87× raw-node | 0.95× | 83 ms | 116 MB |
| ch3 compiled (ELF) | 1.15× raw-node | 1.76× (204k rps) | 3 ms | 4 MB |
| fastify on node | 0.69× | 0.65× | 111 ms | 108 MB |

The compiled build sits at ≥96% of a bare compiled `node:http` server on every cell: the router costs ~0.1-0.3 MB of binary and ~1 MB RSS.

## [Errors](/errors/)

# Errors

```ts
app.onError((err, c) => {
  c.status(500).json({ message: err.message });
});
```

An error thrown anywhere in the chain (middleware, handler, response) lands here.

Fallback behavior:

- No `onError` registered, or the handler never responds, or the handler itself throws: built-in `500 Internal Server Error`.
- Headers already sent: socket destroy.

The built-in `405` error carries `.allow` (the `Allow` header value), so custom bodies are easy:

```ts
app.onError((err, c) => {
  if ("allow" in err) {
    c.status(405).header("allow", err.allow).text("method not allowed");
    return;
  }
  c.status(500).text("boom");
});
```


---

## [ch3](/)

# ch3

A minimal synchronous HTTP router for `node:http` with zero dependencies, authored inside the scriptc compilable subset.

```ts
import { createRouter } from "ch3";

const app = createRouter();

app.get("/", (c) => c.text("hi"));
app.get("/user/:id", (c) => c.json({ id: c.req.param("id") }));
app.post("/echo", (c) => c.text(c.req.body()));
app.notFound((c) => c.status(404).text("not found"));

app.serve({ port: 3000 });
```

## Why

Two reasons:

- Handlers are synchronous. Dispatch pre-buffers request bodies, so there is no await anywhere in the hot path.
- The package obeys the scriptc compilable subset (see [Architecture](architecture.md)), so the exact same source compiles to a native ELF: 3 ms cold start, 4 MB RSS, 204k req/s pipelined on a shared VM.

## Install

```bash
npm i ch3
```

Next: [Routing](routing.md).


---

## [Middleware](/middleware/)

# Middleware

Middleware is synchronous: `(c, next) => void`.

```ts
app.use((c, next) => {
  c.header("x-start", Date.now().toString());
  next();
});
```

Middleware applies to routes registered **after** it (snapshot semantics).

## Body

`c.req.body()` is synchronous because dispatch pre-buffers the request body (`data`/`end` concat) for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE before invoking the chain. Other methods dispatch immediately.

Next: [Errors](errors.md).


---

## [ch3 generated-dispatch contract (\`src/gen.ts\`)](/route-contract/)

# ch3 generated-dispatch contract (`src/gen.ts`)

Status: **frozen** — this is the seam between `ch3` (route table +
ctx machinery) and build-time code generators (the Vite/unplugin transform
agent emits modules satisfying this contract). v0.2.0, 2026-10-11.

## The seam in one paragraph

`app.withDispatch(d)` registers a generated dispatch object. On every
request, `app.serve()`/`app.handler()` calls `d.dispatch(req, res)` **first**.
`true` = the request is handled (or committed to be handled asynchronously
after a body-buffer); `false` = decline — ch3's internal specialized dispatch
takes over. Routes stay registered on `app` either way: the generated module
is a pure accelerator overlay, never a replacement for the route table.

## Module shape

```ts
import { GenDispatch } from 'ch3'

// Emit a CLASS, not an object literal. Under scriptc's eager
// program-code instantiation a function value inside a record
// instantiates the record as `unknown` and fences every call on it;
// class instances with methods compile cleanly. `extends GenDispatch`
// keeps the assignment nominal for both tsc and scriptc.
export class CompiledRoutes extends GenDispatch {
  dispatch(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse): boolean {
    // ... generated matcher ...
  }
}
```

Emitting code then wires it at app construction:

```ts
const app = createRouter()
app.withDispatch(new CompiledRoutes())
// app.get(...) calls still run — the route table stays the source of truth.
```

`GenDispatch` (from `src/gen.ts`, re-exported by `src/index.ts`):

```ts
export class GenDispatch {
  dispatch(req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse): boolean {
    return false
  }
}
```

## Dispatch precedence — deterministic

1. `withDispatch` may be called at most once; a second call **replaces** the
   previous dispatch object (documented, deterministic — last wins).
2. Every request calls `dispatch` exactly once, before any internal work —
   including requests the generated module does not recognize.
3. `false` must only be returned **before** any response bytes, headers, or
   `req.on(...)` listeners are committed. Returning `false` after
   `setHeader`/`end`/body-listeners is a contract violation (undefined
   behavior, double-response).
4. Returning `true` after `app._buffer(...)` was invoked is correct even
   though the response completes later — the commitment is made at
   listener-attach time.
5. The internal dispatch never calls generated code; generated code never
   calls back into `App._dispatch`. One direction only.

## What generated code may use (the stable surface)

Everything below is a **contract member** — it will not change shape in 0.x
without a major-version note. Members not listed are private.

```ts
// Construction: the generated matcher already parses the URL for its own
// matching — pass the pieces through, no double-parse.
const rv = new ReqView(raw, qs, path)   // (req, query-string-w/o-?, path-w/o-?)
const c  = new Ctx(rv, res)

// Params: after the generated matcher binds a route with params, seed the
// lazy param store with decoded name/value pairs — flat array, pairs of 2.
rv._seedPm(['id', dec(segValue)])       // 'id' → param('id'), '*' for splat
// If nothing is seeded, param() materializes from the entry declared on
// the internal table (only when the internal dispatch ran) — generated
// routes that return true MUST seed their own params.

// Body: ONLY for routes the author declared `body: true` at registration.
app-free helper, attaches 'data'/'end', buffers, then runs k under the
// send500 guard. Returns void; dispatch() must still return true.
_buffer(req, res, c, function (): void { handler(c) })

// Guard: wrap synchronous handler execution with the standard 500 path.
_guard(res, function (): void { handler(c) })
```

| Export | Signature | Contract |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| `GenDispatch` | class, `dispatch(req,res): boolean` | subclass + override |
| `ReqView` | `new (raw, qs, path)` | qs/path already split at `?` |
| `ReqView._seedPm` | `(pm: string[]) => void` | flat decoded pairs incl `'*'` |
| `ReqView._setBody` | `(s: string) => void` | set by `_buffer` only |
| `Ctx` | `new (rv, res)` + `json/text/html/status/header/redirect` | unchanged authoring API |
| `App.withDispatch` | `(d: GenDispatch) => App` | last-wins, tried first per request |
| `_buffer` | `(req, res, c, k: () => void) => void` | data/end + `_setBody` + guarded `k` |
| `_guard` | `(res, k: () => void) => void` | `try { k() } catch → send500` |
| `dec` | `(s: string) => string` | `+`→space then `decodeURIComponent`, fallback raw |

## Body buffering — declared-body rule

The request body is buffered **only** when the route declared body use at
registration. This is a hard contract, not a hint:

```ts
app.post('/echo', (c) => c.text(c.req.body()), { body: true })
```

- `body: true` + a body-carrying method (`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`) →
  body is buffered before the handler chain runs; `c.req.body()` returns it.
- `body: true` + `GET`/`HEAD`/etc → no buffering (flag ignored for
  non-carrying methods).
- No declaration → **no buffering, `c.req.body()` returns `''`** — on
  generated and internal dispatch alike. 404/notFound paths never buffer.
- A call-site marker (`ctx.body()` auto-detection) is **rejected**: handler
  introspection is impossible inside the subset (`fn.toString`/`fn.length`
  are SC2020) and would be non-deterministic across the two runtimes. The
  registration flag is the one way to do it.
- `maxBodyBytes` is **not** implemented in v0.2 — document if needed later.

## Rules for emitted code (scriptc subset — same as package internals)

The emitted module compiles into the user's program, so it lives under the
same subset rules as `src/`:

- Sync only. No `Promise`/`async` on the dispatch path.
- `null`, never `undefined`, in every union and return position.
- Class instances (not object literals) for `GenDispatch` impls.
- No function values inside records — generated tables hold `number`
  indices into a class-side `Handler[]` or emit static `if`/`switch`
  dispatch (both compile; `switch` on method strings and flat `if` chains
  are the recommended emit shapes).
- Indexed `for` loops; no `for…in`; no `?.` (use `&&`/`=== null`); no
  spread calls; no `new Function`/`eval`/`Object.create`.
- `String(x)`/`Number(x)` coercion at function entry for `unknown` params.
- `res.end(...)` statement-called. Body accumulation via
  `req.on('data', (c: Buffer) => …)` + `toString()` + `join`, or just call
  `_buffer`.
- `import type` / `.ts` specifiers / `for…of` over arrays / `instanceof`
  vs program classes / class getters / default params all compile clean.

## Versioning

The contract majors with the package: any change to a member listed in the
stable-surface table bumps minor at minimum and is recorded here. The
unplugin agent should pin `ch3` peer ranges accordingly.

## [Routing](/routing/)

# Routing

Routes are registered per method: `app.get | post | put | delete | patch | head | options(path, h)`, plus `app.all(path, h)` for any method and `app.on(method, path, h)` for custom ones.

Paths support static segments, `:param`, and a tail `*` wildcard.

```ts
app.get("/user/:id", (c) => c.req.param("id")); // literal-typed: 'id'
app.get("/wild/*", (c) => c.req.param("*"));
```

## Semantics

- Params are percent-decoded and typed from the path literal (`ParamKey<P>`). Param-less paths degrade `param()` to `string | null`.
- `HEAD` requests fall back to the `GET` handler; node suppresses the body.
- Matched path, unknown method: `405` with an `Allow` header built from the route's method table.
- Unmatched path: `404` (customizable via `app.notFound`).
- Duplicate exact `method`+`path`: first registered wins. Match is strict: no trailing-slash normalization.

## Sub-routers

```ts
const api = createRouter();
api.get("/users", handler);

app.route("/api", api);
```

Parent and sub middleware merge.

Next: [Middleware](middleware.md).


---

## [unplugin-ch3](/unplugin/)

# unplugin-ch3

Build-time route lowering for `ch3`. This is the point of the project's build story: the plugin statically reads your route registrations and emits a specialized dispatch module next to them, so requests skip the runtime trie walk on every match. Everything emitted is authored inside the scriptc-compilable subset, so `scriptc build` lowers it into the native binary.

Full reference: [packages/unplugin/PLUGIN.md](https://github.com/sigilco/ch3/blob/main/packages/unplugin/PLUGIN.md).

## What the plugin does

At `buildStart` (and on each watch event for the file) the plugin scans route modules (default `**/*.ch3.ts`, `**/*.ch3.js`) and emits `.ch3/routes.gen.ts` next to them, satisfying the [generated-dispatch contract](route-contract.md):

- `export class CompiledRoutes extends GenDispatch` whose `dispatch(req, res)` runs per-method sections ordered like the runtime trie (static before param before wildcard, then registration order).
- `routeTable`: full-shape literals `{ method, path, kind, handlerIdx, needsBody }[]`.
- Per-route runners: literal send-chains (`c.json`, `c.text`, ...) compile to straight `res` writes with no `Ctx` allocation; ctx routes build `ReqView`/`Ctx` through the contract surface and call the composed middleware+handler at `app._chains[idx]`.
- `constructor(a: App)` injects the router instance (needed for scriptc lowering; see the scriptc section in PLUGIN.md).

## Bail, not guess

The plugin never silently produces wrong routes. Extracted: literal-path `app.<method>()` calls, `app.all`/`app.on`, `app.use` snapshot semantics, same-file mounts, literal send-chains. Bailed to runtime registration (with a build warning):

- Non-literal paths (variables, calls, spreads).
- Conditional or loop-driven registration.
- Registrations whose handler index cannot be proven against the runtime tables.
- Mounts of routers imported from other modules.

If a routes module cannot be analyzed at all, the plugin emits a stub whose `dispatch` always returns `false`, so the app runs entirely on the runtime path.

## Usage (vite)

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { ch3Plugin } from 'unplugin-ch3'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [ch3Plugin.vite()],
})
```

Mark a routes module:

```ts
// src/routes.ch3.ts
import { createRouter } from 'ch3'

export const app = createRouter()

app.get('/user/:id', (c) => c.json({ id: c.req.param('id') }))
app.post('/echo', (c) => c.text(c.req.body()), { body: true })
```

Wire the generated dispatch:

```ts
// src/main.ts
import { app } from './routes.ch3.ts'
import { CompiledRoutes } from './.ch3/routes.gen.ts'

app.withDispatch(new CompiledRoutes(app))
app.serve({ port: 3000 })
```

`app.serve()` calls the generated dispatch first; `false` declines to the internal dispatch, which covers bails, `notFound`, and misses. Body buffering is opt-in per the contract: a handler reading `c.req.body()` must register with `{ body: true }` or it receives `''`.

The factory is unplugin-based, so `ch3Plugin.rollup()`, `ch3Plugin.webpack()`, and `ch3Plugin.esbuild()` work too. Only vite is verified by a fixture (`fixtures/vite-app/`): run `npm i && npm run build` there, then `node dist/main.js 3100` to hit static, param, middleware, wildcard, bailed, POST-body, and miss routes.
